tidepool

Tidepool is a small command line tool that records water temperature and salinity readings from a field logger and turns them into tidy tables you can plot.

Install

cargo install tidepool

Usage

It reads the logger's CSV export, checks every row against the sensor's documented range, and writes a cleaned file beside the original so nothing is ever overwritten.

tidepool clean logger-export.csv

Readings outside the range are kept in a separate file with the reason they were set aside, so you can decide later whether the sensor or the pool was misbehaving.

Design

The tool has no network access and no configuration file. Everything it needs is given on the command line, and every run prints what it did and where it wrote.

Formats

Exports from three logger families are understood today. Each has its own column order and its own idea of what a missing reading looks like, and the reader for each is a small table rather than a separate parser.

Times are converted to UTC on reading, with the logger's offset kept in a column of its own, so a season of readings taken across a clock change still lines up when plotted.

Testing

Every range in the table has a test that feeds it a reading just inside and just outside the limit. The sample exports in the tests folder are synthetic and were generated for this project.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Please open an issue describing the logger model you use before sending a change, so the range table can be checked against its manual.

The range table lives in one file and every entry cites the page of the manual it came from, so a reviewer can check a change without owning the logger.
